image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) resting on a patch of green grass against a textured grey stone wall. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey-brown body. It is in a tucked, resting posture with its bill pointing towards its back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with the correct yellow-green coloration typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and compact. The plumage texture appears dense and smooth, indicative of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/flank coloring.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is in a resting posture with its legs tucked underneath or hidden by the body and grass; they are not visible for verification.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing the correct contour and feather layering for a broad, pointed wing structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the duck shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (speculum area/tail curl) typical of drakes.

To analyze the fine details of the feather transitions, especially the iridescence on the head and the boundary between the neck ring and breast, for signs of AI smearing.
To ensure the boundary between the duck and the grass/stone background is sharp and that there is no 'melting' or bleeding of the subject into the environment.
To verify the spatial relationship between the duck, the grass foreground, and the stone wall background is physically consistent.

Anatomical correctness of the tucked wing and tail curl
Lighting consistency on the iridescent head
